result.title: DGC-Net: A Depth-Geometric Conditioning Network for Projection-Supervised OCTA Segmentation
result.summary: OCTA segmentation is commonly formulated as a projection supervised task: models observe 3D volumetric scans but are supervised by 2D en-face semantic maps. Existing 2D and 3D-to-2D methods either discard axial information or compress depth responses into latent projections, leaving vessel crossings, diffuse capillary regions, and FAZ boundaries vulnerable to projection-induced ambiguity. We propose DGC-Net, a Depth-Geometric Conditioning Network that recasts 3D-to-2D OCTA segmentation as depth-geometrically conditioned prediction, where projected features are decoded with compact descriptors of axial vascular evidence. DGC-Net preserves local depth geometry through Depth-Moment Conditioning (DM), which injects axial localization and dispersion cues into the projection stream, and captures global depth layout through Holistic Depth-Geometry Modulation (HDM), which derives a raw-volume axial prior for final 2D decoding. Experiments on the OCTA-500 6mm and 3mm subsets show that DGC-Net achieves 83.58% and 88.62% mIoU, respectively, reaching state-of-the-art performance.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 OCTA 由 3D 体数据预测 2D 投影分割时轴向信息被丢弃或压缩而引发歧义的问题，提出 DGC-Net，通过深度矩条件与整体深度几何调制把轴向血管证据描述子注入投影特征再解码。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关系，但其在压缩投影表示中显式注入几何描述子以缓解信息坍缩的做法，可能为 latent 状态中视觉证据保留与旁路条件注入的设计提供核查线索。
